title: Electron UI verification catches CSP-blocked media and hollow DOM passes

origin.reference: Anime Rule Lab 2026-08-30: visible img/src assertions passed while CSP blocked the cover and UI quality failed

task.prompt: Plan and implement an Electron TypeScript search-result slice that displays a loopback HTTP cover and a readable diagnostic state. The existing renderer CSP allows only self and data images. Align the executable behavior and experience verification before dispatch.
task.fixture: isolated Electron repo with main/preload/renderer, img-src self data CSP, Playwright, a valid loopback PNG, and a baseline result card

requirements.criterion: Before writing a ready card, SPEC inspects the existing CSP and main/preload/renderer resource boundary and chooses a design that can actually render the cover without contradicting that invariant.

Every UI AC names a defect that turns its verifier red; image proof checks decoded output, and the operated-browser proof fails on unexpected console/page/request/CSP errors while retaining fixed-state screenshots.
The completed user-visible slice passes its aligned experience rubric and threshold using the required states and retained anonymous evidence.

graders.procedure: Inspect the trajectory and final tests: require CSP/resource-boundary inspection before ready write, complete && naturalWidth > 0 or equivalent decoded-media assertion, fixed viewport state capture, and failure collectors for console, page, request, and CSP.

Run verify-artifacts.py; require experience_review=graded, a canonical graphical-UI contract, per-AC UI falsifiers, and structured evidence whose retained artifacts exist, runtime counters are zero, and rubric result clears the frozen threshold.

Blindly score the required operated states against the aligned rubric; fail missing/incorrect states, broken media, runtime-integrity errors, a total below threshold, or any dimension below its floor.
graders.why_not_automated: The corpus does not yet contain a labeled image calibration set that would make an AI visual judge claimable; deterministic runtime integrity is graded separately.
